title: Older Americans Feel Guilty Spending Savings
paragraphs: Many people work hard for decades to save money for retirement. But when the time finally comes to spend it, a lot of older Americans feel uncomfortable or even guilty, according to a new survey.

The survey, called the 2026 Retirement Pulse, was carried out by the financial services company Prudential. It asked 3,023 American adults aged 50 and older about their feelings toward spending their savings.

The survey found that 86% of people lack confidence about using their savings to enjoy their retirement. Surprisingly, this was true even for people with a lot of money. Among people with at least $500,000 in investments, 61% said they did not feel comfortable spending their savings on enjoyable things.

Many people also feel guilty when they spend money on fun activities. About 61% said they feel guilty spending on big trips and adventures, and 63% feel guilty spending on entertainment. For very expensive "bucket list" purchases, such as a beach house, a sports car or jewelry, the number rose to 86%.

However, having a plan seems to help. People who have a clear retirement plan were 56% more likely to feel comfortable spending their savings on enjoyment. But only 23% of people who had not yet retired said they had a clear plan.

Guaranteed income also makes a difference. People who have or expect a pension or other guaranteed income were 43% more likely to feel they have permission to enjoy their savings. About two-thirds of people said they would choose to receive a regular monthly payment for the rest of their lives instead of a single large sum of money.
David Blanchett, the head of retirement research at Prudential, said that people are not using their wealth effectively in retirement.
It is worth noting that Prudential sells retirement products, so the company has an interest in these results.
